gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold defect is the failure of the Appendix theorem's separate injectivity requirement for Im T at the kappa=0 endpoint, where Im T is the zero operator. ISSUE-002 instead concerns loss of coercivity and an unjustified limit-of-ranges argument for truncated operators when S has zeros; it does not recognise the endpoint injectivity failure or the self-adjoint alternative.

Both entries identify the same failure of the pointwise exponential test function to belong to Range(L) in the old L2(D) formulation: L of an L2 source is an entire Fourier transform that decays on the real axis, whereas equality with the unit-modulus exponential on an open interval would force an impossible global equality. Thus the forward implication in Lemma 3.4 is false.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The old L2(D) operator cannot have the pure exponential in its range: analyticity and decay of Lu contradict the unit-modulus exponential after equality on an open frequency interval, invalidating the claimed range criterion.

component_coverage.gold_component: The pure exponential is not in Range(L) for the stated L2(D) operator, so the forward implication of the pointwise range criterion is false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 gives the same L2-to-L1 pushforward, entire-extension and decay argument, derives the contradiction with the exponential, and explicitly concludes that the 'if' direction of Lemma 3.4 is false.
